claim_ceiling: Reproduction and extension of a two-dimensional Vicsek model with offset restricted visual fields; no claim of biological intelligence, agency or life

publication.title: Influence of visual field offset on collective behavior: An exploration using the two-dimensional Vicsek model
publication.source_scope: A restricted visual field positioned at a fixed offset angle from the particle's heading direction changes which neighbours it can perceive and respond to.

source_dataset.title: Influence of visual field offset on collective behavior: an exploration using the two-dimensional Vicsek model (dataset)
reported_contents: simulation data analyzed in the paper
source_dataset.note: The public page shows a Download All control and a Files heading but no individual file rows in the retrieved rendering. No files have been downloaded. Verify file-level notices, filenames, sizes and digests after lawful acquisition.

reported_findings.key_mechanism: An agent perceives neighbours inside a restricted visual field whose central axis is offset from its direction of motion.

flipped_sensing.definition: Visual-field offset is directly behind the heading direction (π radians).
flipped_sensing.reported_result: Near-perfect alignment and clustering at the centre of mass were reported even under high noise conditions.

reported_findings.interpretation: Perception geometry can qualitatively change collective dynamics; a forward-only sensing assumption is not universal.

current_oli_implementation.range_rule: The existing interaction_radius is retained as the radial visibility limit.
current_oli_implementation.directional_rule: A sees B when B is within range and the bearing from A to B lies within A's visual sector centred at heading_A + offset.
current_oli_implementation.local_metrics: Visible-neighbour counts and local polar order use focal-agent directed out-neighbours.
current_oli_implementation.topology_metrics: Connected components, clustering and path lengths use a weakly connected projection; an undirected edge exists if either direction sees.

benchmark_cases.expected: The visible field is centred along the agent heading; only particles inside the declared forward sector and radial range are visible.
The visible field is centred directly behind the agent heading. Compare collective order and centre-of-mass clustering under source-matched high-noise conditions after exact parameter admission.
A focal particle can see a target while the target does not see the focal particle; directed out-degree is asymmetric, while the topology summary records the weakly connected projection.

source_reproduction_order: Download the public source package and inventory every file.
Record per-file SHA-256, size, file-level licence and source commit/archive identity.
Read the MATLAB README and recover the exact generator, field-of-view width, offset grid, interaction range, density, speed, noise, seeds and transient/stationary measurement window.
Reproduce the original paper's parameter sweep and reported order/clustering results using the authors' original code first.
Implement a Rust-equivalent visual-sector generator and compare trajectory/metric parity on frozen seeds.
Only then add held-out offsets, noise, densities, particle counts, temporal sampling and perturbation tests.
anti_leakage: Keep all frames from one simulated trajectory/seed in one split.
Split by parameter regime and offset, not by frame.
Do not use the paper's reported aggregate result as training data.
Keep forward, side, and flipped sensing as distinct perception geometries in every result row.
When topology metrics are reported, retain the weak-projection semantics and the underlying directed-edge counts.
